validated_results.title: Serum vitamin D concentration and prostate cancer risk: a nested case-control study.
authors: Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial Project Team
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study within the PLCO trial relating pre-diagnostic serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations to incident prostate cancer risk.

extraction.comparison_type: Highest (Q5) vs lowest (Q1) quintile of season-standardized serum 25(OH)D, aggressive prostate cancer
extraction.population: Men in the screening arm of the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial

sample_size.excerpt: The study included 749 case patients with incident prostate cancer who were diagnosed 1-8 years after blood draw and 781 control subjects who were frequency matched by age at cohort entry, time since initial screening, and calendar year of cohort entry.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 749 + 781 = 1530

cases.excerpt: The study included 749 case patients with incident prostate cancer who were diagnosed 1-8 years after blood draw and 781 control subjects who were frequency matched by age at cohort entry, time since initial screening, and calendar year of cohort entry.

effect_size.excerpt: However, serum 25(OH)D concentrations greater than the lowest quintile (Q1) were associated with increased risk of aggressive (Gleason sum > or = 7 or clinical stage III or IV) disease (in a model adjusting for matching factors, study center, and history of diabetes, ORs for Q2 vs Q1 = 1.20, 95% CI = 0.80 to 1.81, for Q3 vs Q1 =1.96, 95% CI = 1.34 to 2.87, for Q4 vs Q1 = 1.61, 95% CI = 1.09 to 2.38, and for Q5 vs Q1 = 1.37, 95% CI = 0.92 to 2.05; P(trend) = .05).

confidence_interval.excerpt: However, serum 25(OH)D concentrations greater than the lowest quintile (Q1) were associated with increased risk of aggressive (Gleason sum > or = 7 or clinical stage III or IV) disease (in a model adjusting for matching factors, study center, and history of diabetes, ORs for Q2 vs Q1 = 1.20, 95% CI = 0.80 to 1.81, for Q3 vs Q1 =1.96, 95% CI = 1.34 to 2.87, for Q4 vs Q1 = 1.61, 95% CI = 1.09 to 2.38, and for Q5 vs Q1 = 1.37, 95% CI = 0.92 to 2.05; P(trend) = .05).

validated_results.title: Legume and isoflavone intake and prostate cancer risk: The Multiethnic Cohort Study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective Multiethnic Cohort analysis reporting dietary legume intake and incident prostate cancer risk with a quantitative relative risk.

extraction.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest intake of legumes, total prostate cancer
extraction.population: 82,483 men in the Multiethnic Cohort Study who completed a quantitative food frequency questionnaire in 1993-1996

sample_size.excerpt: The analyses included 82,483 men who completed a detailed quantitative food frequency questionnaire in 1993-1996. A total of 4,404 prostate cancer cases including 1,278 nonlocalized or high-grade cases were recorded during the average follow-up period of 8 years.

cases.excerpt: A total of 4,404 prostate cancer cases including 1,278 nonlocalized or high-grade cases were recorded during the average follow-up period of 8 years.

effect_size.excerpt: Among men with the highest intake of legumes, the risk reduction was 11% for total prostate cancer (RR = 0.89, 95% CI = 0.80-0.99, p for trend = 0.007) and 26% for nonlocalized or high-grade cancer (RR = 0.74, 95% CI = 0.61-0.90, p for trend = 0.007) compared to men with the lowest intake.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Among men with the highest intake of legumes, the risk reduction was 11% for total prostate cancer (RR = 0.89, 95% CI = 0.80-0.99, p for trend = 0.007) and 26% for nonlocalized or high-grade cancer (RR = 0.74, 95% CI = 0.61-0.90, p for trend = 0.007) compared to men with the lowest intake.
